Synopsis:
    The article covers sterling dynamics against the dollar, driven primarily by BoE rate hike expectations amid an ongoing Middle East conflict (referenced as the "Iran war"). Oil has surged 40% since the war's outbreak, and European natural gas prices are roughly three times higher. Markets price in at least two BoE hikes by March, though Governor Bailey pushes back against any pre-committed rate path. ING flags that each $10/bbl rise in Brent adds ~15bps to UK 2-year rates, more than in the eurozone or US. Near-term uncertainty around oil prices and the UK Autumn Budget keeps ING on the sidelines on sterling.
